title: The Tower of Civilization
gist: A foresight consultant describes turning Stewart Brand's pace layers framework into 'Layer Player,' a Jenga-style block tower sold to CEOs, and uses it to argue that fast, noisy layers (Commerce) carry little systemic power while slow base layers (Nature) destabilize everything when touched. He deliberately re-cut Brand's stack for business audiences — dropping Fashion, elevating Commerce to the top, and placing AI in Infrastructure, one layer above Governance.

themes.theme: Signal hierarchy: slow layers hold the power

insights.claim: In the pace layers model, the fastest-moving layers generate the loudest headlines but the slowest base layers emit rarer signals that actually determine system outcomes — so headline volume is inversely related to signal importance.
insights.speaker: Long Now Foundation
insights.so_what: Reallocate research attention away from high-frequency news flow toward slow variables (resource limits, demographics, legal regimes) where the real regime changes originate.
insights.quote: The base layers, by contrast, have all the power: they move much slower and emit far fewer but much more important signals.
insights.locator: The top layers draw attention because

insights.claim: Disturbing the Nature layer at the base of the stack destabilizes every layer above it, whereas shuffling Infrastructure or Governance blocks can be absorbed without toppling Commerce.
insights.speaker: Long Now Foundation
insights.so_what: Treat ecological and resource shocks as system-wide repricing events rather than sector-specific ones; mid-stack policy or infra churn is usually noise by comparison.
insights.quote: As soon as you touch the largest blocks in the Nature layer at the bottom of the stack, however, the whole tower threatens to come tumbling down.
insights.locator: It’s relatively easy to move a blue block

insights.claim: Change in any single pace layer predictably creates friction with the layers immediately above and below it, making adjacency the map for second-order effects.
insights.speaker: Long Now Foundation
insights.so_what: When a shock lands, look first at the neighbouring layers for the transmission channel rather than at the loudest sector.
insights.quote: Changes in one layer usually create friction with the layers above and below.
insights.locator: One model that consistently resonates with leaders

insights.claim: Commerce has historically grown by discounting planetary boundaries, meaning the Nature layer carries an unpriced liability that sits underneath the entire corporate stack.
insights.speaker: Long Now Foundation
insights.so_what: Frames climate and resource constraint not as an ESG overlay but as deferred cost accruing at the base of every business model.
insights.quote: you can see how Commerce has historically discounted planetary boundaries in pursuit of growth
insights.locator: In interacting with the Layer Player

insights.claim: Rising societal polarization in the Culture layer transmits downward into Governance and then into Infrastructure and Commerce, giving a mechanism by which culture-war dynamics eventually hit corporate operating conditions.
insights.speaker: Long Now Foundation
insights.so_what: Polarization is a leading indicator for regulatory instability and infrastructure delivery risk, not just a media story.
insights.quote: how the increasing polarization of societies in the Culture layer scrapes against Governance, which in turn affects Infrastructure and Commerce
insights.locator: In interacting with the Layer Player

themes.theme: AI classified as Infrastructure, not Commerce

insights.claim: AI belongs in the Infrastructure layer rather than the Commerce layer, which implies it moves slower and matters more structurally than its equity-market narrative suggests.
insights.speaker: Long Now Foundation
insights.so_what: Argues the durable AI value accrues at the infrastructure layer while the fast Commerce-layer AI story is the noisy, less consequential part of the stack.
insights.quote: Or take AI, which I placed in the blue Infrastructure layer.
insights.locator: Or take AI, which I placed

insights.claim: Deploying increasingly capable AI models pushes value up into Commerce while simultaneously creating friction downward into Governance, so AI is a two-directional shock rather than a pure productivity tailwind.
insights.speaker: Long Now Foundation
insights.so_what: Expect the governance/regulatory backlash to be a structural feature of AI diffusion, arriving from the layer directly beneath the technology.
insights.quote: Deployment of increasingly capable AI models clearly moves up the stack to impact Commerce, but at the same time these models create friction down the stack.
insights.locator: Or take AI, which I placed

insights.claim: Advanced AI has direct implications for the leadership systems that manage populations, positioning state governance — not just industry — as the contested surface for frontier models.
insights.speaker: Long Now Foundation
insights.so_what: Watch for AI capability jumps to translate into political-control and state-capacity contests, a slower but more consequential channel than product cycles.
insights.quote: advanced AI clearly has potential implications for leadership systems that manage populations
insights.locator: Governance is immediately below the Infrastructure layer

insights.claim: The plexiglass sleeve holding the block tower together represents an era of stability with little inter-layer movement, and that era is explicitly described as over.
insights.speaker: Long Now Foundation
insights.so_what: A stated regime call: models calibrated on low inter-layer friction (stable governance, stable trade, stable climate) are now mis-specified.
insights.quote: It embodies an era of stability, with little movement between layers and few sparks between systems. The world is no longer in that era.

insights.claim: Once inter-layer constraints are removed, shocks ricochet both up and down the stack rather than propagating in one direction, which is why single-layer analysis understates fragility.
insights.speaker: Long Now Foundation
insights.so_what: Stress-test scenarios in both directions — regulation hitting technology and technology hitting regulation — rather than assuming a single causal arrow.
insights.quote: you begin to grasp the fragility of systems, and how ricochets can reverberate up and down the layers

themes.theme: Frameworks fail on distribution, not content

insights.claim: The binding constraint on strategic frameworks reaching decision-makers is retention, not comprehension — the model is understood in the room and then discarded.
insights.speaker: Long Now Foundation
insights.so_what: Explains why research that is analytically correct still fails to change allocation decisions; packaging is the leverage point.
insights.quote: While the framework clicks, it doesn’t stick.

insights.claim: The operative success metric for executive communication is being impossible to file and easy to share, a test that written reports structurally fail.
insights.speaker: Long Now Foundation
insights.so_what: A reusable heuristic for anyone whose product is influence over senior decision-makers: optimize for unfileability, not thoroughness.
insights.quote: Success was a simple metric: impossible to file and easy to share.

insights.claim: In a 2012 government engagement, a mandated written report was immediately absorbed into an aide's pile while a self-standing tent card of three recommendations stayed on a Cabinet Minister's desk for six weeks and was carried into senior-official meetings.
insights.speaker: Long Now Foundation
insights.so_what: Concrete evidence that physical form, not content quality, determined which output actually influenced policy discussion.
insights.quote: the tent card didn’t fit in his shelves, so he put it on his desk
insights.locator: Once the Minister returned to his office

insights.claim: CEOs in a cohort of ten non-competing firms began a 2025 foresight engagement with limited comprehension of foresight and even less understanding of complex system interactions — senior corporate literacy on systemic risk is low.
insights.speaker: Long Now Foundation
insights.so_what: If boards cannot model cross-layer interactions, expect corporates to be systematically late repricing governance, trade, and climate shocks.
insights.quote: The CEOs had limited comprehension of foresight, and even less understanding of the complex system interactions shaping the world.
insights.locator: At the start of 02025, my team began work

insights.claim: The specific topics executives needed briefing on were the implications of fast-moving technologies on governance and the friction between national or grand strategies and free trade — identifying tech-governance and strategy-versus-trade as the live cross-layer fault lines.
insights.speaker: Long Now Foundation
insights.so_what: A read on what a foresight practitioner considers the two dominant macro frictions to brief boards on in 2025.
insights.quote: the implications of fast-moving technologies on governance, for example, or the friction between national/grand strategies and free trade
insights.locator: We needed to get them up to speed

insights.claim: Brand's Fashion layer was deleted from the physical model and Commerce promoted to the top purely to win business-leader engagement, meaning the artifact encodes an audience bias rather than a corrected theory.
insights.speaker: Long Now Foundation
insights.so_what: A caution for consumers of any strategy framework: the version circulating in boardrooms may have been edited for palatability, dropping the layer that signals fastest.
insights.quote: I also removed Fashion as a layer.
insights.locator: I also removed Fashion as a layer

insights.claim: Block size in the model was made proportional to each layer's influence on the system, so the three Nature blocks at the base are the largest and the top blocks a fraction of their size.
insights.speaker: Long Now Foundation
insights.so_what: Makes explicit the weighting the author assigns: ecological constraint dominates the system, commerce is the least load-bearing layer.
insights.quote: the size of the blocks would be relative to their influence on the system
insights.locator: Each of the pace layers would have its own color

insights.claim: Sedimentary layers and onion metaphors were discarded as physical analogies because no design would persuade a CEO to give up desk space for boxes or dirt — the metaphor had to survive an aesthetic and status filter, not just an analytical one.
insights.speaker: Long Now Foundation
insights.so_what: Illustrates that adoption of a mental model is filtered by executive status signalling as much as by explanatory power.
insights.quote: Sedimentary layers and onions were quickly discounted.

insights.claim: The model had to be playable, not merely viewable, because the core lesson — that excessive change in the base layers destabilizes everything above — only lands through physical manipulation.
insights.speaker: Long Now Foundation
insights.so_what: Interactive simulation beats exposition for transferring systems intuition; relevant to how risk is communicated to boards and clients.
insights.quote: If the base layers change too much, for example, all the layers above suddenly become unstable.
insights.locator: The physical object also had to encourage people to play
